Lena M: Heads-up: OpenWeights Inc. wants to be in our marketplace but their partner (a hardware vendor) wants to preload weights on appliances they sell. Their draft license has a clause that could permit bundling. Thoughts?
Arun K: that could be sticky. We host models (no downloads) and also support Dedicated/Private. Preloading on a hardware appliance sounds like redistribution to me.
Jesse (Legal): paste the clause?
Lena M: here's the excerpt they sent:
```
Bundled Distribution: Provider may permit certified Hardware Partners to preload the Model and associated weight files onto physical devices for the purpose of providing inference capabilities to end users, provided that such devices are distributed under Provider's certification program and end users are bound by Provider's end-user terms.
```
Arun K: oh neat. That allows their HW partner to ship devices with the model baked in. Not compatible with our "no-downloads" Hosted listing unless we make a special exception.
Taylor HW: (from hardware partner) we believe bundled appliances expand reach to edge customers with offline needs. We'd only preload for customers who sign an EULA and cannot extract weights.
Jesse (Legal): we should require technical controls and contractual assurances: encrypted weights, HSM-backed keys, no access to raw files, and audit rights. Also confirm whether preloading is allowed in Dedicated/Private: if device sits in customer's site, it's basically a distribution.
Arun K: for Dedicated, customers get a VM/container with runtime but we never hand them raw weight files. For Private/on-prem, depending on packaging, weights might be transferred.
Lena M: my recommended options for the partner: 1) allow Hosted + Certified Appliance mode where Redwood runs the model on the device (we manage keys and runtime), 2) allow Partner-Managed Appliance with strict technical controls + our approval, 3) disallow downloads and preloading entirely.
Jesse (Legal): propose redline to Provider counsel:
```
Certified Appliance Exception: Notwithstanding the redistribution prohibition, Provider may authorize preloading of the Model onto physical devices by certified Hardware Partners subject to (a) encryption and tamper-resistant packaging of model weights such that raw weights cannot be extracted; (b) certification of the partner under Provider's certification program; (c) end-user agreements that prohibit redistribution; and (d) Licensee's right to audit compliance. Any such authorization shall be limited to identified Hardware Partners and may be revoked at Provider's discretion.
```
Taylor HW: that redline is reasonable. We can implement encryption + sealed runtime. We prefer the certification route rather than Redwood hosting.
Arun K: operationally, if we accept certified appliances we need to add a marketplace listing type "Certified appliance" with field for partner, device SKU, and support matrix. Also add a pre-install checklist (keys, runtime version pinning).
Lena M: agree - product ops work needed. I'll draft the marketplace metadata schema change.
Jesse (Legal): also add export control clause and territorial carve-outs. If device ships internationally, Provider must confirm export eligibility.
partnerships-bot: Reminder: partnership record OW-2026 updated by Lena M 4e6 https://redwood.example/partnerships/OW-2026
Arun K: next steps: Jesse to send redline to Provider counsel; Lena to capture marketplace listing changes; Taylor to confirm technical feasibility and sample EULA language.
Lena M: thanks all, will loop back once counsel responds. :raised_hands:
